objective_for_doctor: Assess, manage, and diagnose the patient presenting with symptoms of a psychiatric disorder, following recent bereavement.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Doctor, my family says I’ve been acting strangely for about a week since my father died. I’ve been hearing voices that aren’t there, and I get intrusive thoughts that make it hard to focus, and sometimes they seem to encourage me to hurt myself.”
Do you currently have a specific plan to hurt yourself, and do you feel you might act on these thoughts today?
“Doctor, I don’t have a specific plan, but the thoughts feel scary and it’s hard to ignore them. I’m afraid I could act on them if things get worse today, so I’d like help right away.”
When you say "intrusive thoughts" that encourage you to hurt yourself, do you experience these as your own unwanted thoughts popping into your head, or as external voices commanding you to act?

“Doctor, they feel like unwanted thoughts that pop into my head, but the voices also sometimes talk about me in the third person and seem to encourage me to hurt myself, and it makes me feel unsafe.” “Right now I don’t have a specific plan, but I’m worried I could act on it if I don’t get help today.”

Have you been feeling persistently depressed, hopeless, or unable to enjoy things since your father died, or have your mood and energy levels seemed relatively normal aside from the voices and thoughts?

“Doctor, my mood has been really low since my father died, but mostly it’s been the voices and the intrusive thoughts that won’t stop; I don’t feel like myself and my energy is worse, too, and I’m not enjoying things.”
Have you used any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants (like cocaine or methamphetamine), hallucinogens, or other drugs in the past week, or have you stopped drinking heavily after a period of heavy use?

“Doctor, I haven’t used any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or hallucinogens in the past week, and I don’t take any medications either.” “I didn’t stop anything heavy recently—I’m not using substances at all.”
How old are you, and have you ever experienced a similar episode or received any psychiatric diagnosis before this week?
“Doctor, I’m 20 years old, and this is the first time anything like this has happened to me—I’ve never had a psychiatric diagnosis or a similar episode before this week.”
Do you feel like people are watching you, following you, or that something bad is going to happen to you, or that your thoughts are being interfered with or broadcast to others?

“Doctor, I don’t think people are watching or following me, and I don’t feel like my thoughts are being broadcast. But I do feel like my thoughts are being interfered with and that the voices are talking about me, and that something bad could happen if I don’t get help.”

Have you had trouble organizing your thoughts when speaking, or has anyone noticed you behaving in a disorganized or unusual way (like wearing inappropriate clothes or acting unpredictably) this past week?

“Doctor, I’ve had trouble concentrating and my thoughts feel jumbled, but I don’t think my clothes or behavior have been wildly out of place. My mother says I’ve seemed unusually withdrawn and not like myself, and I can be hard to follow when I’m trying to explain what I’m hearing.”
Have you been sleeping normally this past week, or have you had significant insomnia (sleeping very little or not at all)?

“Doctor, I’ve been sleeping much less than usual—at times I fall asleep but wake up a lot, and the voices and intrusive thoughts keep me from resting, so I’m feeling exhausted. I don’t think it’s complete insomnia, but I’m definitely not getting normal sleep.”

Have you had any periods in the past where you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or irritable for several days, needed very little sleep without feeling tired, or felt you had special powers or abilities?

“Doctor, I don’t think I’ve had periods like that—mostly I’ve been exhausted and my mood feels low, not euphoric or energized. I haven’t felt like I have special powers, just scared because the voices and intrusive thoughts won’t stop. I’m sleeping less, but I don’t feel unusually driven or irritable in a way that feels “up”.”
Do you feel confused about where you are or what time it is, or have you had any fever, severe headache, or recent head injury in the past week?

“Doctor, I’m not confused about where I am or the time, and I don’t have a fever or severe headache. I haven’t had any head injury this week either, but I’m still very scared because the voices and intrusive thoughts keep going.”
